title: Credential orchestration lab: visual assets for API key scoping, streaming & tool-calls
creator: Ava Chen
description: Design and deliver a compact 'Credential Orchestration Lab' asset suite for the API/SDK quickstart. Assets should teach developers how to: create scoped API keys, enable streaming, and configure tool-calling permissions. Deliverables include static screenshots for docs, an animated micro-demo GIF (streaming token lifecycle), an accessible SVG sequence for key scoping, and code snippet overlays for JS/Python SDKs. Goal: reduce time-to-first-success by making auth and permission concepts explicit with visuals that can be embedded in docs and in-console help.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Four export-ready assets: key-scoping SVG (small/large), streaming GIF (looped, 8s max), tool-call sequence PNG frames (3), and one composite screenshot for the Quickstart hero. 2) All images have alt text and accessible captions. 3) Copy approved by PM. 4) Figma file includes slices with naming convention DES-21547_<asset>_v1.png/svg/gif. 5) Assets uploaded to Drive + linked in the ticket. 6) Engineering signoff on SDK code overlays for accuracy.

design_notes: Prefer vector SVGs for the key-scoping diagrams to ensure crispness at multiple sizes; include a 2x PNG export for legacy embedding.
Animated streaming demo should avoid autoplaying audio and be under 8s; include a single-frame poster image for small-screen docs.
Tool-calling visuals show permission modal, sample tool call, and result card — simplified to three frames to reduce cognitive load.
Keep overlays minimal: code font Source Code Pro, 14px, with subtle drop shadow to remain readable over screenshots.
Provide dark-mode variants; use tokenized colors to prevent divergence from product styling.
review_feedback: Priya Kapoor (PM): 'Love the onboarding-first approach. Please replace the 'all-access' example with a scoped example before finalizing.'
Liam O'Neill (Eng): 'Code snippets look good. Please update the JS streaming example to use the latest cursor API and add a one-line comment about fallback behavior if KV cache is cold.'
Sofia Patel (Security): 'No secrets in images. Ensure all screenshots redact real keys and that sample keys follow dev-key-* pattern.'
